enum.name: MAV_AUTOPILOT
enum.description: Micro air vehicle / autopilot classes. This identifies the individual model.

entry.name: MAV_AUTOPILOT_GENERIC
entry.description: Generic autopilot, full support for everything

entry.name: MAV_AUTOPILOT_GENERIC_WAYPOINTS_ONLY
entry.description: Generic autopilot only supporting simple waypoints

entry.name: MAV_AUTOPILOT_GENERIC_WAYPOINTS_AND_SIMPLE_NAVIGATION_ONLY
entry.description: Generic autopilot supporting waypoints and other simple navigation commands

entry.name: MAV_AUTOPILOT_GENERIC_MISSION_FULL
entry.description: Generic autopilot supporting the full mission command set

entry.name: MAV_AUTOPILOT_INVALID
entry.description: No valid autopilot, e.g. a GCS or other MAVLink component

enum.name: MAV_TYPE
enum.description: MAVLINK component type reported in HEARTBEAT message. Flight controllers must report the type of the vehicle on which they are mounted (e.g. MAV_TYPE_OCTOROTOR). All other components must report a value appropriate for their type (e.g. a camera must use MAV_TYPE_CAMERA).

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_GCS
entry.description: Operator control unit / ground control station

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TAILSITTER_DUOROTOR
entry.description: Two-rotor Tailsitter VTOL that additionally uses control surfaces in vertical operation. Note, value previously named MAV_TYPE_VTOL_DUOROTOR.

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TAILSITTER_QUADROTOR
entry.description: Quad-rotor Tailsitter VTOL using a V-shaped quad config in vertical operation. Note: value previously named MAV_TYPE_VTOL_QUADROTOR.

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TILTROTOR
entry.description: Tiltrotor VTOL. Fuselage and wings stay (nominally) horizontal in all flight phases. It able to tilt (some) rotors to provide thrust in cruise flight.

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_VTOL_FIXEDROTOR
entry.description: VTOL with separate fixed rotors for hover and cruise flight. Fuselage and wings stay (nominally) horizontal in all flight phases.

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TAILSITTER
entry.description: Tailsitter VTOL. Fuselage and wings orientation changes depending on flight phase: vertical for hover, horizontal for cruise. Use more specific VTOL MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TAILSITTER_DUOROTOR or MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TAILSITTER_QUADROTOR if appropriate.

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_VTOL_TILTWING
entry.description: Tiltwing VTOL. Fuselage stays horizontal in all flight phases. The whole wing, along with any attached engine, can tilt between vertical and horizontal mode.

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_GENERIC_MULTIROTOR
entry.description: Generic multirotor that does not fit into a specific type or whose type is unknown

entry.name: MAV_TYPE_ILLUMINATOR
entry.description: Illuminator. An illuminator is a light source that is used for lighting up dark areas external to the sytstem: e.g. a torch or searchlight (as opposed to a light source for illuminating the system itself, e.g. an indicator light).

enum.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG
enum.description: These flags encode the MAV mode.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG_SAFETY_ARMED
entry.description: 0b10000000 MAV safety set to armed. Motors are enabled / running / can start. Ready to fly. Additional note: this flag is to be ignore when sent in the command MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE and MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM shall be used instead. The flag can still be used to report the armed state.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG_HIL_ENABLED
entry.description: 0b00100000 hardware in the loop simulation. All motors / actuators are blocked, but internal software is full operational.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG_STABILIZE_ENABLED
entry.description: 0b00010000 system stabilizes electronically its attitude (and optionally position). It needs however further control inputs to move around.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG_GUIDED_ENABLED
entry.description: 0b00001000 guided mode enabled, system flies waypoints / mission items.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG_AUTO_ENABLED
entry.description: 0b00000100 autonomous mode enabled, system finds its own goal positions. Guided flag can be set or not, depends on the actual implementation.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_FLAG_TEST_ENABLED
entry.description: 0b00000010 system has a test mode enabled. This flag is intended for temporary system tests and should not be used for stable implementations.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_CALIBRATING
entry.description: System is calibrating and not flight-ready.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_STANDBY
entry.description: System is grounded and on standby. It can be launched any time.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_ACTIVE
entry.description: System is active and might be already airborne. Motors are engaged.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_CRITICAL
entry.description: System is in a non-normal flight mode (failsafe). It can however still navigate.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_EMERGENCY
entry.description: System is in a non-normal flight mode (failsafe). It lost control over parts or over the whole airframe. It is in mayday and going down.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_POWEROFF
entry.description: System just initialized its power-down sequence, will shut down now.

entry.name: MAV_STATE_FLIGHT_TERMINATION
entry.description: System is terminating itself (failsafe or commanded).

enum.name: MAV_MODE
enum.description: These defines are predefined OR-combined mode flags. There is no need to use values from this enum, but it simplifies the use of the mode flags. Note that manual input is enabled in all modes as a safety override.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_PREFLIGHT
entry.description: System is not ready to fly, booting, calibrating, etc. No flag is set.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_STABILIZE_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under assisted RC control.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_STABILIZE_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under assisted RC control.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_MANUAL_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under manual (RC) control, no stabilization

entry.name: MAV_MODE_MANUAL_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under manual (RC) control, no stabilization

entry.name: MAV_MODE_GUIDED_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control, manual setpoint

entry.name: MAV_MODE_GUIDED_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control, manual setpoint

entry.name: MAV_MODE_AUTO_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control and navigation (the trajectory is decided onboard and not pre-programmed by waypoints)

entry.name: MAV_MODE_AUTO_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control and navigation (the trajectory is decided onboard and not pre-programmed by waypoints)

entry.name: MAV_MODE_TEST_DISARMED
entry.description: UNDEFINED mode. This solely depends on the autopilot - use with caution, intended for developers only.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_TEST_ARMED
entry.description: UNDEFINED mode. This solely depends on the autopilot - use with caution, intended for developers only.

message.name: HEARTBEAT
message.description: The heartbeat message shows that a system or component is present and responding. The type and autopilot fields (along with the message component id), allow the receiving system to treat further messages from this system appropriately (e.g. by laying out the user interface based on the autopilot). This microservice is documented at https://mavlink.io/en/services/heartbeat.html
message.field: Vehicle or component type. For a flight controller component the vehicle type (quadrotor, helicopter, etc.). For other components the component type (e.g. camera, gimbal, etc.). This should be used in preference to component id for identifying the component type.
Autopilot type / class. Use MAV_AUTOPILOT_INVALID for components that are not flight controllers.
A bitfield for use for autopilot-specific flags
MAVLink version, not writable by user, gets added by protocol because of magic data type: uint8_t_mavlink_version

message.name: HIL_CONTROLS
message.description: Sent from autopilot to simulation. Hardware in the loop control outputs
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.

message.name: HIL_ACTUATOR_CONTROLS
message.description: Sent from autopilot to simulation. Hardware in the loop control outputs (replacement for HIL_CONTROLS)
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.
Control outputs -1 .. 1. Channel assignment depends on the simulated hardware.
Flags as bitfield, 1: indicate simulation using lockstep.

message.name: HIL_SENSOR
message.description: The IMU readings in SI units in NED body frame
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.
Angular speed around X axis in body frame
Angular speed around Y axis in body frame
Angular speed around Z axis in body frame
Bitmap for fields that have updated since last message
Sensor ID (zero indexed). Used for multiple sensor inputs

message.name: HIL_GPS
message.description: The global position, as returned by the Global Positioning System (GPS). This is NOT the global position estimate of the system, but rather a RAW sensor value. See message GLOBAL_POSITION_INT for the global position estimate.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.
0-1: no fix, 2: 2D fix, 3: 3D fix. Some applications will not use the value of this field unless it is at least two, so always correctly fill in the fix.
GPS HDOP horizontal dilution of position (unitless * 100). If unknown, set to: UINT16_MAX
GPS VDOP vertical dilution of position (unitless * 100). If unknown, set to: UINT16_MAX
GPS ground speed. If unknown, set to: UINT16_MAX
GPS velocity in north direction in earth-fixed NED frame
GPS velocity in east direction in earth-fixed NED frame
GPS velocity in down direction in earth-fixed NED frame
Course over ground (NOT heading, but direction of movement), 0.0..359.99 degrees. If unknown, set to: UINT16_MAX
Number of satellites visible. If unknown, set to UINT8_MAX
GPS ID (zero indexed). Used for multiple GPS inputs
Yaw of vehicle relative to Earth's North, zero means not available, use 36000 for north

message.name: GNSS
message.field: GNSS velocity north in mm second
GNSS velocity east in mm second
GNSS velocity down in mm second
